patch_description: Replace part of the isotropic random coordinate proposals with directions derived from the currently most restrictive incident triangles.  For a limiting triangle containing the moving point, its area changes most directly by moving that point along the normal to the opposite edge; choosing the sign away from that edge increases its altitude.  Additional directions repel the point from its nearest neighbors, helping resolve clustered low-area triples.  Random directions are retained for escaping competing-constraint local traps.  This makes the same proposal budget substantially more aligned with the determinant-area objective, especially in late-stage refinement.
